title: Settings

catalog.title: Model catalog
catalog.description: Shared reference metadata with local, per-field overrides. A card does not make a model callable.
catalog.name: Model / variant
catalog.valueHint: Enter a value; use Unknown or Inherit explicitly
catalog.listHint: Comma-separated; empty means an explicit empty list
catalog.priceNote: USD per million tokens. 0 is free; blank is not zero. Reference estimates are not channel billing prices.
catalog.patchHint: Only edited fields are saved. Inherit removes this level's override, not values from other levels.
catalog.readOnly: Read-only. Only instance administrators may edit metadata or updates.
catalog.affects_one: Changes to this base model affect {{count}} variant.
catalog.affects_other: Changes to this base model affect {{count}} variants.
catalog.duplicateId: This ID already exists. Open that entry to edit its fields instead.
catalog.bindingRequired: Select the model/provider scope and enter an upstream ID
catalog.conflict: This snapshot is stale (409). Your edits have not been saved. Refresh, close and reopen to review the latest values; no automatic overwrite.
catalog.deleteConfirm: Remove metadata for {{id}}? This does not delete the connection, usage history or billing.
catalog.protected: {{count}} local override records remain protected across updates.
catalog.noMatch: No catalog identity matched. Unknown fields are not inferred from the name.

subagentPoolReasoningEffortHelp: Only affects newly created subagents. A specified tier overrides the agent's input and is adapted to model support. Not specified applies no pool override; it is not none (thinking off).
instanceAdminOnlyHint: Your account is not an administrator. Instance configuration such as provider management is only available to admin accounts. Please sign in with an admin account to configure it.
integrationsDescription: See connected apps, plugins, remote devices, ownership, and runtime health in one place. Detailed controls remain in their dedicated settings pages.
integrationsLoadFailed: Could not load the integration summary
integrationsCapabilityCatalogDescription: {{oauth}} OAuth capabilities and {{plugin}} plugin capabilities are normalized into the shared catalog, with {{shared}} canonical capabilities available through both integration paths.
integrationsConnectedAppsDescription: OAuth grants approved by your account.
integrationsPluginsDescription: Installed extensions, compatibility, and runtime health.
integrationsOAuthAppsDescription: Third-party clients registered for External API access.
integrationsDevicesDescription: Executor connectivity and externally owned devices.
integrationsResourcesDescription: Devices and narrators created by connected applications.
integrationsAttention_plugin_attention: One or more plugins are degraded, failed, quarantined, or incompatible.
integrationsAttention_orphaned_resources: OAuth-created resources have lost their active grant and are safely disabled.
integrationsAttention_offline_devices: One or more remote devices are offline.
grammarsIntro: StructView reads files by their structure — outlines, symbol bodies, public APIs — and StructSed changes them at the same addresses. Accurate results need a language parser, downloaded on demand rather than shipped in the binary to keep the download small. Without it, StructView falls back to text heuristics and says so, and StructSed's symbol addressing is unavailable (line and regex addresses still work).
grammarsTierVerifiedHint: These languages have a hand-written declaration table, so outlines and symbol extraction are exact.
grammarsTierGenericHint: These parse correctly, but structure is inferred from cross-language node-type rules, so some declaration forms will be missing. StructView says so in its output.
grammarsBuiltinHint: Ships with the app and is always available. Shell parsing is used to analyse every command NarraFork runs, so it is never downloaded and cannot be removed.
grammarsDigestMismatchHint: The cached file no longer matches the expected checksum. Re-download to restore accurate parsing.
grammarsRemoveConfirmMessage: Remove the {{label}} grammar? StructView will fall back to text heuristics for this language until it is downloaded again.
grammarsSourceNote: Parsers are fetched from a pinned package on a public CDN and verified against a built-in SHA-256 checksum before use. A file that fails verification is discarded, never loaded.
devicesDescription: Register and diagnose remote executors, choose which projects may use them, and route narrator tools to other machines.
deviceDeleteConfirmMessage: Revoke "{{name}}"? Its token stops working and any live connection is dropped.
deviceSlugDescription: Narrators and executor commands can reference this identifier. Leave blank to generate it from the name.
deviceSlugInvalid: Use 2–64 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores.
deviceModeReverseDescription: Recommended behind NAT: the executor opens an outbound authenticated WebSocket to NarraFork.
deviceModeDirectDescription: NarraFork dials the executor. Public/non-loopback listeners must use TLS and the executor still needs its device token.
deviceDirectUrlDescription: Network connections must use wss://. Unencrypted ws:// is accepted only for 127.x.x.x or [::1] loopback addresses.
deviceDirectUrlInvalid: Enter a wss:// URL, or ws:// with a loopback IP literal.
deviceScopeGlobalDescription: Every project and standalone narrator may select this device.
deviceScopeProjectDescription: Only narrators belonging to the selected project may select this device.
deviceEditReconnectHint: Changing connection mode or URL reconnects the device. Changing scope immediately affects which narrators may select it.
deviceDiagnosticsLoadFailed: Could not load the current diagnostic state.
deviceTokenWarning: This token is shown only once. Copy it now and store it securely.
deviceRunHint: Run the executor on the device with a command like:
deviceTokenFileHint: Before running the command, save the token to a permission-restricted file (chmod 600 on Unix). Secret managers may instead pipe it to an executor started with --token-stdin.
deviceRotatedNextStep: The previous token stopped working immediately. Update the token file on the device and restart the executor service, or run the install command again.
devicePlaintextEnrollmentLabel: Allow automatic key delivery over plaintext http on a private network
devicePlaintextEnrollmentHelp: Off by default. The one-line installer lets the target machine fetch its device key, which over https is encrypted and over plaintext http is not. Enabling this accepts that the key crosses your local network in the clear once, at enrollment. Public addresses are never covered: plaintext http on a routable address always refuses to hand out a key. Only literal IP addresses count as a private network; hostnames are never eligible, because the server cannot verify which network a name resolves to.
executorInstallIntro: Builds one command for "{{name}}" that installs executor v{{version}} as a service. The device key is never written into the command.
executorInstallNoRelease: No published executor release was found. Check the update server URL in settings, or build and publish the executor first.
executorInstallNoPty: Windows ConPTY is not supported yet, so this device cannot host interactive terminals. File, search, transfer and Git operations work normally.
executorInstallModeHelp: A system service starts at boot under a dedicated account. A user install runs under your own account and needs no administrator rights.
executorInstallPathGuardLater: Path rules are configured after installation, on the device page, where you can browse the machine's real directories. Until you add rules, the executor may reach any path its OS account can reach.
devicePathRulesHelp: An ordered allow/deny list. Rules are checked from the bottom up and the last matching rule wins, so a deny can carve an exception out of an allow, and a later allow can re-open a subdirectory inside that deny.
devicePathRulesOrderHelp: Order matters: the last matching rule decides. A path matching no rule is refused.
devicePathRulesUnrestricted: No rules: the executor may reach any path its OS account can reach. Add rules to limit file, search and transfer operations. Note this is a path guard, not a shell sandbox.
devicePathRulesSaved: Path rules saved. Apply them on the device to take effect.
devicePathRulesApplyHelp: Saving here records your intent only. The executor reads its rules from its own config file, which is what keeps the guard effective even if this server is compromised. Merge this into the device's config.json and restart the executor service.
devicePathRulesDriftHelp: The device reports enforcing different rules than the ones saved here. Apply the config on the device and restart the executor service.
executorInstallDisableShellHelp: Removes the Bash and PTY surfaces. File, search, transfer and Git operations remain available.
executorInstallRunOneLiner: Run this on the target machine ({{shell}}):
executorInstallRunWith: Equivalent to saving this as {{filename}} and running it with {{shell}}:
executorInstallTokenReminder: The script will prompt for the device key. Input stays hidden and the key is stored in a permission-restricted file.
executorInstallEnrollNotice: The command collects the device key itself, so there is nothing to paste. It works once and expires shortly; collecting the key also replaces it, so if someone else runs the command first, your run fails instead of quietly sharing a key.
executorInstallTicketExpires: This command expires at {{time}}. Generate a new one if it lapses.
executorInstallServerUrl: Server URL the device will use
executorInstallServerUrlHelp: Defaults to the address you are using now. Change it if the target machine reaches NarraFork by a different name, for example over a VPN or with split-horizon DNS.
executorInstallServerUrlLoopback: This is a loopback address. It works from this browser but is unreachable from any other machine — set the address the target machine can actually reach, unless you are installing onto this very host.
executorInstallTokenDeliveryHelp: Automatic gives you a single command to paste. Manual keeps the key out of the command entirely and asks you to type it during installation.
executorInstallTokenDeliveryUnavailable: Automatic delivery is unavailable over plaintext http on a public address, because the device key would cross the internet unencrypted. Serve NarraFork over https, or install with manual key entry. On a private network an administrator can allow it with the checkbox at the bottom of this settings page — but only for a literal IP address; a hostname is never eligible, because the server cannot verify which network it resolves to.
executorInstallRevealKeyHelp: Manual installs need the key on hand. Stored keys are hashed and cannot be read back, so this issues a new one.
executorInstallKeyRotatedNotice: This replaced the device's previous key. Shown only now.
loginMethodsDescription: Ways to sign in to your account. These are independent of two-factor authentication.
mfaSectionDescription: Require a second step at sign-in for extra protection.
mfaRequireDescription: When on, sign-in asks for a second factor after your password. You can use an authenticator app or a registered passkey.
mfaNoFactorHint: Add an authenticator app or a passkey below before you can require two-factor sign-in.
mfaDisabledSuccess: Two-factor sign-in is no longer required
mfaFactorsHint: Registered passkeys can also be used as a second factor when two-factor sign-in is required.
totpEnrollEnableMfa: Require two-factor at sign-in after setup
totpEnrollEnableMfaHint: Recommended. You can change this later in the two-factor section.
totpDescription: Add a second step to sign-in using a time-based code from an authenticator app like Google Authenticator, 1Password, or Authy.
totpScanInstruction: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app.
totpVerifyInstruction: Enter the 6-digit code shown in your authenticator app to confirm.
totpDisableConfirm: Disable two-factor authentication? Your account will be less secure.
totpDisableInstruction: To disable two-factor authentication, confirm your identity with a current code or your password.
backupCodesWarning: Store these one-time codes somewhere safe. Each can be used once to sign in if you lose access to your authenticator. They will not be shown again.
passkeyDescription: Sign in without a password using your device's biometrics or a security key. Passkeys can also serve as a second factor.
passkeyUnsupported: This browser or connection does not support passkeys. Passkeys require a secure context (HTTPS or localhost).
passkeyDeleteConfirm: Remove this passkey? You won't be able to sign in with it anymore.
ssoDescription: Link an external identity provider to sign in without a NarraFork password.
ssoUnlinkConfirm: Unlink this identity provider from your account?
ssoProvidersDescription: Configure OpenID Connect providers. Each enabled provider adds a sign-in option on the login page.
ssoProviderDeleteConfirm: Remove this SSO provider? Users linked to it will no longer be able to sign in with it.
ssoFieldDomainsHint: Comma-separated. Leave empty to allow any domain.
ssoAllowSignupHint: Create a local account on first login when no identity is linked. Independent of the registration switch and of registration codes: while this is on, anyone the provider authenticates can get an account even with registration closed. Restrict who that is with the allowed email domains above. Accounts created this way always get the regular user role.
ssoValidationRequired: Provider ID, name, issuer and client ID are required.
ssoValidationId: Provider ID must be lowercase letters, digits, hyphens or underscores.
ssoValidationIssuer: Issuer must be a valid http(s) URL.
ssoValidationSecret: A client secret is required for a new provider.
webauthnDescription: Optional. Leave blank to auto-derive from each request, which works for localhost and LAN access. Set these only when serving on a fixed domain behind a reverse proxy.
webauthnRpIdHint: A domain, e.g. narrafork.example.com (no scheme or port).
avatarFileTooLarge: Avatar image is too large. Please choose a file smaller than {{max}}.
serverHostDesc: The address the server listens on. Changes take effect immediately.
settingsLooseValidationWarning: Settings validation is running in loose JSON mode.
settingsLooseValidationWarningDesc: This backend normalizes settings before saving them instead of applying the TypeScript Zod schema strictly. Double-check provider, TLS, and agent values after saving.
settingsPatchUnsupportedWarning: Settings saving is unavailable in this backend runtime.
settingsPatchUnsupportedWarningDesc: This backend reports settings patch support as disabled, so changes cannot be safely saved here.
settingsSecretMaskingUnsupportedDesc: This backend reports that settings responses may not mask secrets. Avoid exposing this page in shared screenshots or logs.
providerAgentModeUnsupportedTitle: Some providers cannot run agent sessions
providerAgentModeUnsupportedDesc: The current backend reports agent mode as unavailable for: {{providers}}. Their models are hidden from agent model selectors but remain visible in provider settings.
chapterSplitUnsupported: Chapter split is not available in this backend runtime.
chapterContainersUnsupported: Container settings are not available in this backend runtime.
chapterContainersAsyncStartDesc: This backend returns from container start requests immediately and streams startup progress through logs/status updates instead of waiting synchronously for compose to finish.
runtimeBenchmarkContainerExecutionUnsupp: Benchmark container execution is not available in this backend runtime.
runtimeVNetUnsupported: Virtual network support is not available in this backend runtime.
runtimeVNetModeInfo: VNet is running in {{mode}} mode. UDP rendezvous: {{udp}}.
sendModeDesc: Choose the queue behavior each send key triggers when the narrator is running
brandingSubSectionDesc: Distinguish this instance from other NarraFork deployments. Applies to everyone using this server.
brandNameDesc: Shown in the browser tab, the installed app name, the app header and the sign-in page. Leave blank to use NarraFork.
brandIconColorDesc: Recolours the favicon, the installed app icon and the notification icon.
updateServerUrlDesc: URL of the update server (e.g., https://updates.example.com)
openBrowserDesc: How to open the browser when the server starts. Restart required to take effect.
translationModelDesc: Model used to translate reasoning blocks. Follows the summary model by default.
promptOptimizeModelDesc: Model used to optimize and refine prompts. Follows the summary model by default.
promptOptimizeContextMaxMessagesDesc: Maximum number of context messages (1-50) to include when optimizing prompts. Default is 3. More context improves optimization quality but uses more tokens.
customModelsDesc: Built-in models cannot be edited or removed. Add custom model IDs below. Click the eye icon to hide a model from selectors.
maxTurnsDesc: Maximum number of agent loop turns per user message (0 = use default)
subagentModelsDesc: Default models for explore, plan, search, and review subagents. Leave empty to inherit from the parent narrator's model.
subagentAllowedModelsDesc: Restrict which models each subagent type can use. Leave empty to allow all models.
customApiProvidersSectionDesc: Configure custom API endpoints that speak Anthropic, Codex, OpenAI Responses, or Chat Completions protocols.
customApiProviderPrefixDesc: Used in model IDs, e.g. "deepseek:deepseek-chat" or "anthropic:claude-sonnet". Any text is allowed except an ASCII colon.
customApiUserAgentDesc: Which User-Agent header to send with requests to this provider. Useful when a gateway expects a specific client identity.
fingerprintDesc: Control how requests identify themselves to the provider: the User-Agent, extra headers, and Codex CLI header emulation.
fingerprintUserAgentDesc: Which User-Agent to present on outbound requests. Selecting NarraFork also sets the Codex originator header to narrafork.
fingerprintExtraHeadersDesc: Additional request headers sent with every request.
fingerprintInstallationIdDesc: A persistent UUID sent as x-codex-installation-id. Regenerate to rotate this identity.
customApiProtocolDesc: Select the protocol this endpoint actually implements. Switching between Anthropic and OpenAI-style protocols automatically migrates the provider type while keeping name, prefix, key, and base URL.
customApiProtocolAnthropicOfficialDesc: Connect to the official Anthropic API or an official relay. Enables Claude Code protocol features, including server-side search, beta flags, prompt caching, and Bearer auth.
customApiProtocolAnthropicCompatibleDesc: Connect to a third-party Anthropic Messages API-compatible gateway. Keeps the standard message format and avoids official-API-only extensions.
customApiProtocolCodexNativeDesc: Connect to a native Codex or Codex reverse-proxy endpoint. Uses the Responses endpoint format, Codex headers, reasoning effort, and optional WebSocket. Recommended for all GPT5.x models to enable thinking intensity settings.
customApiProtocolResponsesCompatibleDesc: Connect to an OpenAI Responses API-compatible endpoint. Best for GPT-4o and newer models, the official OpenAI API, or gateways that implement Responses format.
customApiProtocolCompletionsCompatibleDe: Connect to a Chat Completions-compatible endpoint. Best for GPT-4 and older models, local/Chinese models, Ollama, or gateways that only implement /chat/completions.
customApiProtocolGeminiCompatibleDesc: Connect to Google's Gemini API or a compatible relay, then explicitly choose generateContent or Interactions transport below.
geminiTransportDesc: No automatic probing or fallback is performed. Existing and missing settings use generateContent; /interactions is used only when explicitly selected.
geminiTransportGenerateContentDesc: Compatibility default. Uses /models/{model}:generateContent and :streamGenerateContent, suitable for Google AI Studio and third-party relays that implement the established Gemini API.
geminiTransportInteractionsDesc: Opt-in transport. Sends requests to /interactions and requires the endpoint to implement the Gemini Interactions API.
geminiDefaultReasoningEffortDesc: Default thinking budget for Gemini models when a narrator does not set one. None disables thinking; higher levels raise the thinking token budget.
prefixDuplicate: "{{prefix}}" is already used by another provider
openaiResponsesApiDesc: Enable to use the OpenAI Responses API message format (for official API and Codex-compatible gateways). Try disabling if tool calling doesn't work.
openaiCodexAccountIdDesc: Optional. Sent as ChatGPT-Account-Id header for organization subscriptions.
openaiCodexWebSocketDesc: Use Responses WebSocket instead of HTTP for Codex requests (experimental; falls back to HTTP when unavailable)
openaiCodexWebSearchDesc: Send the native web_search tool to Codex models. Disable this to omit that tool from requests.
openaiCodexImageGenerationDesc: Send the native image_generation tool to supported Codex models. Disable this to omit that tool from requests.
saveBeforeRefreshMessage: This provider has unsaved changes. NarraFork needs to save them before refreshing the model list.
openaiRefreshModelsDesc: Fetched models will appear in all model selectors across the app.
anthropicProxyDesc: Proxy for all requests to this provider. Leave empty for direct connection.
anthropicTlsRejectUnauthorizedDesc: Disable certificate verification for MITM proxies or self-signed certs. Not recommended for production.
anthropicNativeSearchDesc: On by default for Claude Code (official API) providers; turn off if this endpoint does not serve Anthropic's server-side web_search tool. Search runs as a separate one-shot request (Claude CLI style), so prompt caching of the main conversation is never affected.
anthropicRefreshModelsResolvedUrl: Models fetched using a different URL
openaiModelsFromFallbackUrl: Model list fetched from a fallback URL (chat base URL may not need changing)
modelListItemsTruncated: Showing {{shown}} models; {{hidden}} more hidden. Search to narrow the list.
anthropicMaxModeDesc: Mimic Claude Code CLI protocol. Uses Bearer token auth, mcp_ tool prefixing, and ?beta=true endpoint.
nugProvidersSectionDesc: Configure NUG (Narrafork Unified Gateway) endpoints for unified multi-channel AI access
nugProviderPrefixDesc: Used in model IDs, e.g. "nug:claude-sonnet". Any text is allowed except an ASCII colon.
nugEgressModeDesc: Where requests to the AI provider exit to the network. Local modes relay encrypted traffic through this machine; account credentials stay on NUG.
nugEgressAllowFallback: Fall back to NUG-direct when the local egress is offline
nugApiKeyPlaceholder: NUG API Key or login to obtain one
nugLoginDesc: Login to your NUG account at {{url}} to automatically obtain an API Key.
nugLoginTooltip: Login to NUG to obtain an API Key
nugOAuthTooltip: Authorize via OAuth (opens NUG in browser)
nugOAuthError_state_expired: Authorization session expired or server restarted. Please try again.
nugOAuthError_missing_params: Missing authorization parameters. Please try again.
treeSnapshotsEnabledDesc: Capture a content-addressed snapshot of the whole worktree around tool calls and external edits, as the precise rollback boundary. On very large worktrees (e.g. game modpack directories) the scan can slow tool execution noticeably; when off, rollback degrades to per-file replay. Structural snapshots (fork/merge/restore) are unaffected.
proxyEnabledDesc: Route container traffic through a unified reverse proxy using subdomains instead of exposing individual host ports. Requires Podman 5.0+ with pasta network backend.
proxyPortDesc: Port for the reverse proxy server
freshShellEnvDesc: Source user shell profile on each Bash tool execution to get the latest environment variables. Enable this if you modify shell config (e.g. .bashrc, .zshrc) after starting the server.
legacyEncodingDesc: Auto-detect and preserve non-UTF-8 file encodings (e.g. GBK, Shift_JIS). Enable this when working with legacy codebases.
translateReasoningDesc: Translate AI thinking/reasoning content into your language after each block completes. The translation model is configured on the Models page and follows the summary model by default. Both original and translated text are stored.
requestDumpEnabledDesc: Persist the raw request and response data for every AI provider call into request history so you can inspect the full payload later. Takes effect for subsequent requests in the current session immediately after save — no need to interrupt or restart the narrator. Requests already in flight without collection cannot be backfilled.
requestDumpErrorsOnlyDesc: When enabled, dumps are still collected while a request runs, but only failed requests are saved to request history; successful requests are discarded. Like the master switch, this applies to subsequent requests immediately after save.
requestDumpWarningBody: When enabled, NarraFork will persist raw request and response dumps for every AI provider call, which may quickly consume significant disk space. Turn this on only while debugging request issues, and turn it off when debugging is complete.
defaultNarratorVisibilityDesc: Applies only to newly created narrators; existing narrators are unchanged. Forks inherit their source's permissions. Auto keeps standalone sessions private and chapter sessions visible to the project. Public sessions are visible to all signed-in users. Private sessions are accessible only to their owner. Write permissions are determined by the separate default write audience setting.
defaultNarratorWriteAudienceDesc: Applies only to newly created narrators; existing sessions are unchanged. Forks inherit their source's permissions. Auto follows visibility (existing behavior). Owner allows only the owner; administrators and explicit grants still follow existing rules. Project allows project members with write access. Public allows all signed-in users who meet project access requirements. This global write audience never expands visibility and is automatically narrowed at creation to the range allowed by effective visibility.
defaultNarratorWriteAudiencePublic: All signed-in users with project access
defaultStartInPlanMode: Start new narrators in plan mode
defaultStartInPlanModeDesc: Enable the plan-mode trait by default for new narrators. Permission mode remains a separate safety policy.
defaultRelaxedPlanDesc: Enable relaxed plan mode by default for new narrators. In relaxed plan mode, tools remain available while planning instead of being disabled.
planModeAllowInlinePlanDesc: Allow plan mode to submit plans inline via the ExitPlanMode plan parameter. When off, only the file-based plan flow is supported: the ExitPlanMode schema, its description, and the plan-mode system reminder drop the inline option, and plans are read only from the designated plan file.
planReflectionAutoApproveDesc: Sessions that inherit the global default skip manual approval after ExitPlanMode plan reflection confirms the plan.
planReflectionAllowAutoCompact: Allow plan reflection to reset context
planReflectionAllowAutoCompactDesc: When auto-approving plans, allow plan reflection to choose approval with a context reset so the plan is stored in Conversation Context before execution. Disabled by default.
questionReflectionEnabledDesc: When enabled, AskUserQuestion in Bypass All mode is automatically answered and submitted by reflection after the timeout.
questionReflectionTimeoutDesc: How long AskUserQuestion waits before automatic reflection answers it (seconds). Default is 300 seconds.
dangerReflectionLevelDesc: Controls which risk levels trigger a danger-reflection pause in Bypass All mode. Medium pauses medium and higher risks; Light pauses only clearly dangerous operations and lets unknown/unclassified Bash and writes confined to system temp directories (such as /tmp) through; Strict pauses every classified risk.
dangerReflectionEnabledDesc: Sessions that inherit the global default run a second reflection confirmation for high-risk operations in Bypass All mode.
dangerSkipReadOnlyConfirmationsDesc: When enabled, proven read-only operations in Bypass All mode no longer trigger an extra safety pause. Edit is treated as recoverable and usually won't pause; deletions, clearly dangerous execution patterns, environment injection, unanalyzed/unclassified Bash, and external writes touching user paths are still evaluated by the current danger reflection level. External writes confined to system temp directories (such as /tmp) rank as medium, so the Light level no longer pauses them.
autoContinuationModeDesc: Controls whether the agent automatically continues when spec tasks remain unfinished after a turn ends.
maxTransientRetriesDesc: Maximum retry attempts for transient API errors (rate limits, server errors). Set to -1 for infinite retries.
maxToolCallsPerResponseDesc: Maximum tool calls in a single model response (integer 1–128, default 32). Exceeding this limit automatically aborts the narrator. This is not a cumulative limit across the entire session.
silentToolCallThresholdDesc: After this many tool calls without visible text content, inject a sidecar asking the model to briefly say what it is working on. Set to -1 to disable.
pipelineUnusedToolCallThresholdDesc: Automatically clear Pipeline captures before the next non-Pipeline tool call after this many calls without ExtractPipeline using them. Set to -1 to disable.
behaviorFenceIntervalDesc: Inject the behavior fence via a sidecar every N completed tool calls (skipped when the fence is empty). Set to -1 to disable. Global default; each narrator can override it in the behavior-fence panel.
tasksReminderIntervalDesc: Inject the tasks.json reminder via a sidecar every N completed tool calls. Minimum is 5; set to -1 to disable. Global default; each narrator can override it in the auto-continuation panel.
behaviorFenceAttachTasks: Attach behavior fence to task reminder (default)
behaviorFenceAttachTasksDesc: When enabled, inject the behavior fence alongside the tasks.json reminder. Global default; each narrator can override it.
retryBackoffCeilDesc: Maximum wait time (seconds) for exponential backoff. Retry delay will not exceed this value.
firstTokenTimeoutDesc: Abort and retry if no meaningful AI API event (text, tool, reasoning, web search, image generation, queue event) arrives within this many seconds after request dispatch. Set to 0 to disable.
customRetryRulesDesc: Define custom rules to treat specific API errors as retryable. Matching errors will be automatically retried instead of failing immediately.
customRetryRulesUnsupported: Custom retry rules are not supported by the current backend runtime.
retryRuleAtLeastOne: At least one of domain, status code, or keyword is required
contextThresholdsDesc: Configure when compaction triggers, split by model context window size.
autoCompactKeepPairsDesc: Number of recent user/assistant turns to keep after automatic compaction. Each turn keeps a user/assistant pair.
queueDuringCompactionDesc: While the narrator is compacting its context, a newly-sent message is queued (editable and cancellable) and its turn starts automatically once the compaction finishes. When off, the message is sent immediately, concurrently with the compaction. Either way, the send menu lets you cut in and run immediately. On by default.
compactStartDesc: Trigger context compaction when context usage reaches this value. Defaults: standard 95%, large 75%.
globalWhitelistDirsDesc: Directories auto-allowed for all narrators. Project and narrator level can add more.
globalBlacklistDirsDesc: Directories blocked for all narrators. Takes priority over whitelist.
globalCommandWhitelistDesc: Commands auto-allowed for all narrators. Supports glob patterns (e.g. npm*, docker*).
globalCommandBlacklistDesc: Commands auto-denied for all narrators. Takes priority over whitelist. Supports optional deny prompt.
cmdDenyPromptPlaceholder: Optional: message returned to AI when denied...
oledModeDesc: Use pure black background in dark mode for AMOLED displays to save power and reduce smearing
pluginThemeDesc: Apply a color theme contributed by an installed plugin
autoLoadOlderMessagesDesc: Automatically load earlier messages when scrolling to the top of a conversation
replyInUserLanguage: Ask Narrator to reply in your language
replyInUserLanguageDesc: Instruct the Narrator to respond in the same language as your UI
addSubagentToRecentTabsDesc: Automatically add subagent (child narrator) to sidebar tabs when opening it
showTokenUsageDesc: Display input/output token counts after each conversation turn
showOutputStatsDesc: Display a live chars/sec indicator in the header bar, averaged over a 3-second window
ignoreSafeAreaDesc: Hide the system status bar and use the entire screen. Turn off to show the status bar.
wakeLockDesc: Prevent the screen from dimming or locking while NarraFork is open
advancedAnimationDesc: Enable blur-in for newly appearing user messages, tool call cards, and reasoning cards
blurInDurationDesc: How long the blur-in runs for newly appearing cards. Set to instant to skip it while keeping advanced animation on. Does not affect the per-character fade of streaming text.
streamTokenDurationDesc: How long each character's fade-in runs as text streams in. Set to instant for text that appears immediately. The fade starts fully transparent, so this is also how long freshly arrived text stays unreadable. Above about 1s a fast stream may fade faster than set: only a bounded number of characters can animate at once, so the oldest finish early.
narratorCenteredColumnDesc: Cap the narrator message column at a centered 860px reading width instead of filling the window.
lodAltGestureDesc: Hold Alt while scrolling (or pinch on touch) to change how much detail narrator messages render with; holding Alt also shows the level indicator. Turn off to make Alt do nothing — use the detail-level entry in the narrator toolbar instead.
mockStreamPanelDesc: Show a temporary harness in the narrator dock that replays scripted reasoning / text / tool output for tuning list animations. Nothing is persisted.
expandReasoningDesc: Automatically expand reasoning/thinking blocks in narrator messages instead of showing them collapsed
pwaForceUpdateDesc: Refresh PWA cache and reload the page. Note: This does not check for backend server updates, only refreshes the frontend cache.
overviewModelPreviewTruncated: Showing {{shown}} models in this preview; {{hidden}} more hidden. Open provider details or search the model list to manage more.
overviewHiddenPreviewTruncated: Showing {{shown}} hidden models in this preview; {{hidden}} more hidden.
addProviderModalDesc: Start with the protocol format your endpoint actually supports. For Chinese models or third-party relays that support Anthropic Messages, prefer Anthropic Compatible. After creation, fill in the prefix, API key, base URL, and default model.
addProviderAnthropicCompatibleDesc: Connect third-party gateways or model services compatible with the Anthropic Messages protocol without enabling official-API-only extensions.
addProviderAnthropicCompatibleHint: Recommended first for Chinese models; tool calling and long context are usually more stable.
addProviderCompletionsDesc: Connect OpenAI-style endpoints compatible with /chat/completions, best for older models, local models, and gateways that only implement Completions.
addProviderCompletionsHint: Choose this when the endpoint does not support Responses or Anthropic Messages.
addProviderResponsesDesc: Connect endpoints compatible with the OpenAI Responses API, best for GPT-4o and newer models or gateways with full Responses support.
addProviderResponsesHint: Requires the endpoint to support Responses format and the related tool-calling protocol.
addProviderCodexDesc: Connect native Codex or Codex reverse-proxy endpoints using Responses format, Codex headers, and reasoning effort settings. Recommended for all GPT5.x models to enable thinking intensity settings.
addProviderCodexHint: Best for dedicated Codex proxies and recommended for GPT5.x models.
addProviderClaudeCodeDesc: Connect the official Anthropic API or an official relay with Claude Code protocol features such as beta flags, prompt caching, and server-side search.
addProviderClaudeCodeHint: Choose this only for the official Anthropic API or endpoints explicitly compatible with Claude Code protocol.
addProviderNugDesc: Use NarraFork Unified Gateway to access multi-channel AI services with gateway-side quota, routing, and health management.
addProviderNugHint: Best for team gateways and multi-channel routing.
addProviderGeminiDesc: Connect to Google Gemini or a compatible relay. generateContent is the compatibility default; Interactions is an explicit opt-in transport.
addProviderGeminiHint: Choose the transport implemented by your endpoint; no automatic fallback is attempted.
geminiSectionDesc: Configure Google Gemini endpoints. Paste an API key from Google AI Studio, fetch the model list, then pick the models to enable.
geminiProviderPrefixDesc: Used in model IDs as {prefix}:model. Must be unique across providers.
geminiApiKeyPlaceholder: Paste your Google AI Studio API key
geminiModelPickerDesc: Choose which models from this provider are available for use.
geminiModelPickerEmpty: No models — click Fetch Models first
modelAggregationsSectionDesc: Group the same model from different providers into a single virtual entry. Switch providers or use auto-routing when selected.
aggRoutingPriorityDesc: Use the first available provider in order
aggEmpty: No model aggregations. Add one to get started.
aggSubmitHint: Enter a name and select at least one model
aggMemberOrderPriorityDesc: Drag or use the arrows to reorder. The topmost model is tried first.
aggMemberOrderBalancedDesc: Order sets the round-robin starting sequence across members.
customModelsSectionDesc: Manually add model IDs that aren't auto-discovered by providers above.
orphanCustomModelsSectionDesc: Custom models whose provider is no longer configured.
notifyOnDoneDesc: Trigger notification when a narrator in your sidebar tabs completes its task
notifyOnWaitingDesc: Trigger notification when a narrator is waiting for permission approval
notifyPwaEnabledDesc: Show system notifications via the browser Notification API
notifySoundUploadDesc: MP3, WAV, OGG, or WebM, max 1MB
notifySoundVolumeDesc: Playback volume for notification sounds. 0% mutes them.
notifySoundMaxConcurrentDesc: Extra notifications arriving while this many sounds are already playing are dropped, so a burst does not stack into a loud overlap.
notifyDingtalkSecretDesc: Optional. HMAC-SHA256 signing key for the custom bot
notifyFeishuSecretDesc: Optional. Signature verification key for the custom bot
commandsSectionDesc: Define custom slash commands that expand into prompt templates. Type /commandName in the chat input to use them.
commandPromptPlaceholder: Enter the prompt text. Use {{paramName}} as placeholders for named parameters.
commandDescriptionPlaceholder: Brief description shown in the autocomplete list
commandRunBashFirstDesc: When enabled, using this command runs the Bash command below via the /bash flow before sending the prompt to AI. The Bash result is included in the same AI turn context.
commandBashCommandPlaceholder: e.g. git status --short. Supports {{input}} and parameter placeholders.
commandEmpty: No commands defined. Add one to get started.
commandDuplicateName: A command with this name already exists
commandInvalidName: Command name can only contain letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores
commandModelOverrideDesc: Switch to a different model when this command is used
codexAuthDesc: Sign in with your ChatGPT account to use Codex models. No API key needed.
codexProxyDesc: Proxy for all Codex requests (OAuth and API). Leave empty for direct connection.
codexRemoteHint: Browser login is only available when accessing NarraFork locally. Use device code login for remote/headless servers.
codexWaitingBrowser: Waiting for browser authorization... Complete the login in the opened window.
codexDeviceCodeInstructions: Enter this code on the OpenAI website:
codexDescription: Manage multiple ChatGPT accounts for Codex models. Credentials are stored locally and support automatic failover.
codexGlobalProxyDesc: Default proxy for all Codex requests. Can be overridden per credential.
agentDefaultReasoningEffortDesc: The single default reasoning effort applied to every model. A narrator's own setting overrides it; unsupported tiers are clamped to the nearest tier the model supports. Defaults to max.
reasoningEffortBlocklistDesc: Effort is sent to every model by default (Claude before 4.6 is excluded by a built-in rule). Add a model here when its upstream rejects the parameter — the tier menu then hides for it. Plain text matches the model id as a case-insensitive substring; /regex/ is also accepted.
reasoningEffortBlocklistEmpty: No exclusions — every model receives a reasoning effort hint.
codexUseWebSocketDesc: Use Responses WebSocket instead of HTTP for Codex requests (experimental; falls back to HTTP when unavailable)
codexUseWebSearchDesc: Send the native web_search tool to Codex models. Disable this to omit that tool from requests.
codexUseImageGenerationDesc: Send the native image_generation tool to supported Codex models. Disable this to omit that tool from requests.
codexImportDesc: Paste JSON containing refresh_token/access_token, sub2api-style account exports, comma/newline-separated refresh tokens, or account lines containing rt_xxxxx / email----pass----at----access_token. Email is extracted when present. Access-token-only accounts are imported but will not refresh AT. Codex personal access tokens (at-...) and Agent Identity exports (agent_identity with agent_runtime_id + agent_private_key) are also supported.
codexImportNoValidTokens: No valid refresh or access tokens found
codexCredentialsArchivedDesc: Retired from the pool: never selected for requests, but usage data and stats are kept.
codexLifetimeCostNote: Cost is at OpenAI's official API prices. A ChatGPT subscription is not billed per token, so this is equivalent consumption, not money spent.
codexLifetimeCostPartial: {{count}} requests used a model with no known price and are not included in the cost.
codexTierOrderDesc: Drag to set the account tier order used by tier-balanced mode. Higher tiers are tried first; accounts within the same tier are balanced. Unknown tiers are last.
codexBrowserCallbackDesc: The authorization redirects to {{redirectUri}}, which resolves on the machine running the browser. If the browser does not finish authorization on its own (the callback page fails to load, or NarraFork runs on another host), copy the full URL from the address bar and paste it here.
codexBrowserCallbackServerDown: The local callback server ({{redirectUri}}) failed to start, so the browser will show an unreachable page after authorization. That's fine — copy the full URL from the address bar and paste it below to finish.
codexDeleteConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this credential?
credentialBatchDeleteConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete {{count}} selected credentials?
credentialDeleteUnhealthyConfirm: Delete all {{count}} credentials disabled for too many failures or banned status? This applies across all pages.
codexBrowserAuthStarted: Browser authorization started. Complete the login in the opened window.
codexDeviceAuthInstructions: Visit the verification URL and enter this code:
codexModelsDesc: Backend built-in model list. Click the eye icon to hide a model from selectors. Add custom models in the Custom Models section below.
codexResetCreditConsumeConfirm: Consume 1 reset credit to immediately restore this account's quota windows?
codexResetCreditConsumeSuccess: Quota reset: {{windowsReset}} window(s) restored, {{remaining}} reset credit(s) left
codexResetCreditConsumeTooltip: Consume 1 reset credit to restore quota windows now ({{count}} left)
codexResetCreditNoCredits: No reset credits available — query usage to refresh
codexManagerParityWarning: Codex manager runs in partial parity mode.
codexManagerParityWarningDesc: Some Codex manager scheduler or usage queue semantics differ from the TypeScript backend. Capability-specific controls are disabled when the backend reports them as unsupported.
codexUsageQueueClearUnsupported: Usage queue clearing is not available in this backend runtime.
codexQuotaOverviewDesc: Known usage for {{known}} accounts; {{missing}} accounts still need usage data.
codexQuotaOverviewCoverageDesc: Modeled quota for {{modeled}} accounts; {{unmodeled}} accounts cannot be modeled and {{missing}} still need usage data.
codexQuotaNoTierSelected: Select at least one tier to view quota data.
codexQuotaNoTierWithAccounts: No accounts yet. Tiers appear here once credentials are added.
codexQuotaTrendEmpty: No trend yet. Query or use Codex accounts to collect reset times.
routinesDesc: Enable or disable built-in commands and skills available in the slash menu
toolModeAutoPending: Toolsearch is not implemented yet, so Auto currently behaves the same as Manual.
depsInstallNeedsSudoPassword: This install needs a sudo password, which cannot be entered automatically. Opened a terminal so you can type it.
depsInstallConfirmMessage: The following command will be executed:
depsDelegateHint: Not sure which command fits this machine? A narrator can probe the system and install the missing dependencies for you. You choose how much authority it gets.
depsDelegateNothingToDo: Nothing to install — all supported dependencies are already present
depsDelegateFailed: Could not start the setup narrator: {{error}}
depsAuthorizeTitle: How much should the narrator be allowed to do?
depsAuthorizeDesc: The narrator will probe this machine and install the missing dependencies. Choose how much authority it gets — you can switch the permission mode from the narrator's toolbar afterwards.
depsAuthorizeStandardDesc: Every command that changes the system waits for your approval. Slower, but you see and confirm each step.
depsAuthorizeFullDesc: Commands run without per-command approval, so setup completes unattended. Risky-looking commands still get a self-review step, but that is the narrator checking its own work, not you — some commands will run without you seeing them first. Only choose this if you are comfortable letting it run shell commands on this machine.
depsAuthorizeSudoNote: Either way, the narrator can never enter a sudo password. When one is needed it will run the command in a terminal and ask you to type the password in the terminal panel (the terminal button in the narrator's status bar).
depsAuthorizeSelfInstall: No thanks, I'll install them myself
depsRgDesc: Fast code search for AI tools
wizardWelcomeDesc: This wizard will help you configure the essential settings to get started. You need to complete all steps before using NarraFork.
wizardDepsDesc: NarraFork relies on a few system tools. Check that the required ones are installed.
wizardDepsOptionalHint: You can skip this step. Missing Git only affects project and version-control features, and a narrator can install it later.
wizardProviderDesc: NarraFork needs at least one AI provider to power its narrators. You can configure providers in the admin panel.
wizardBasicDesc: Set the default project directory, preferred AI model, and summary model.
wizardCompleteDesc: You're ready to go. Create a project or start a standalone narrator session to begin.
wizardProviderRequired: You must configure at least one AI provider before proceeding
wizardModelsRequired: Both default model and summary model must be configured
wizardSummaryModelDesc: Used for title generation, context compaction, and other background tasks
wizardNetworkDesc: Choose whether NarraFork should only be accessible on this machine, or open to your local network.
wizardNetworkLocalDesc: Listen on localhost — only this computer can access NarraFork. More secure.
wizardNetworkLanDesc: Listen on your LAN IP — devices on the same network can access NarraFork, but not the wider internet.
wizardNetworkOpenDesc: Listen on 0.0.0.0 — other devices on your LAN can access NarraFork.
wizardNetworkRestartHint: Changes take effect when you finish — the page will reload at the new address.
summaryModelUnavailableDesc: The configured summary model is not available. Features like title generation and context compaction require a working summary model.
summaryModelUnavailableHint: Please select a new summary model below.
summaryModelErrorDescIntro: An error occurred while calling the summary model. Features like title generation and context compaction may not work. You can switch to a different model below.
brokenModelMigrationDesc: These narrators are pinned to a model that can no longer run, usually because its provider was removed or disabled. Pick a replacement model and migrate them in one go.
brokenModelMigrationEntry: Migrate narrators with an unusable model →
brokenModelMigrationEntryDesc: Find narrators still pinned to a removed or disabled provider and move them to a working model.
brokenModelMigrationNoneFound: No narrator is pinned to an unusable model.
brokenModelMigrationTruncated: There are more affected narrators than can be listed here. Migrate these first, then scan again.
brokenModelMigrationMaybeUsableHint: These models are not in the catalog but may still work — some gateways accept any model id. Not selected by default.
brokenModelMigrationUndoHint: Only the most recent migration can be undone. Narrators you changed afterwards are left as they are.
baseUrlFixDescription: The base URL for "{{provider}}" is missing the /v1 path. We automatically corrected this request to keep it working, but long conversations may fail intermittently until the setting is fixed. Permanently update the configuration?
tlsEnabledDesc: Serve over HTTPS using TLS certificates. Requires a valid certificate and private key file. Changes trigger a server restart.
tlsCertFileDesc: Path to the PEM-formatted TLS certificate file (e.g., fullchain.pem)
tlsKeyFileDesc: Path to the PEM-formatted TLS private key file (e.g., privkey.pem)
tlsPassphraseDesc: Passphrase for the private key (leave empty if not encrypted)
tlsPassphraseSecurityWarning: This value is stored in plain text. Use file permissions to restrict access.
tlsCaFileDesc: Path to the CA certificate file (optional, overrides default trusted CAs)
tlsGenerationUnsupported: TLS certificate generation is not supported by the current backend runtime.
tlsGenerateSuccess: Certificate issued and HTTPS enabled. Server is restarting...
serverRestartRequired: Settings saved, but the server must be restarted for the change to take effect.
tlsGenerateWarning: Other devices must import and trust the CA certificate once (see the trust guide). Re-issuing the server certificate never requires re-trust.
tlsCaStatusMissing: Root CA: not created yet (created automatically on first issuance)
tlsLegacySelfSignedHint: The current certificate is a legacy self-signed one. Click "Re-issue with current SANs" to migrate to CA mode — future SAN changes then require no re-trust on devices.
tlsCustomSansDesc: Extra hostnames or IPs used to reach this server, e.g. nas.local, 192.168.1.10, *.home.arpa. Re-issue the certificate to apply changes.
tlsCustomSansPlaceholder: Type a hostname or IP and press Enter
tlsSanInvalid: Invalid entries: {{entries}}. Use hostnames (e.g. nas.local, *.home.arpa) or IP addresses.
tlsCaDownloadError: Failed to download the CA certificate
tlsRegenerateCaConfirm: Regenerating the root CA invalidates the CA trusted on every device — you must download and import the new CA certificate everywhere. Continue?
tlsCaRegenerated: Root CA regenerated and the server certificate re-issued with the stored SANs. Re-import the CA certificate on all devices.
tlsTrustGuideIntro: Trusting this server on another device is a one-time CA import (narrafork-ca.pem):
tlsTrustGuideSteps_windows: Pick "Place all certificates in the following store" → "Trusted Root Certification Authorities"
Finish the wizard, accept the security warning, then fully restart Chrome
tlsTrustGuideSteps_macos: Double-click narrafork-ca.pem to import it into Keychain Access (prefer the "System" keychain)
Double-click the certificate in Keychain Access and expand "Trust"
Set "When using this certificate" to "Always Trust"
Close the window, confirm with your password, then restart Chrome
tlsTrustGuideSteps_linux: Switch to the "Authorities" tab and click "Import"
Select narrafork-ca.pem and check "Trust this certificate for identifying websites"
tlsTrustGuideSteps_ios: Open narrafork-ca.pem in Safari or AirDrop it to the device to download the profile
Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings
Enable full trust for the certificate
tlsTrustGuideSteps_android: Copy narrafork-ca.pem to the phone storage
Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate (or search "certificate" in Settings)
Choose "CA certificate", accept the warning, and pick the file
modelTestResultTruncated: Output preview was truncated to keep the UI responsive.
modelTestSourceError: Narrator error that triggered this test
modelTestVerboseWarning: This model test writes HTTP verbose diagnostics to server stdout or the systemd journal. Header names and diagnostic-safe values are retained; credentials, query secrets, and all unknown header values are redacted.
modelTestResponseBodyTruncated: Body excerpt was truncated; credentials are redacted.
modelTestHint_http: The upstream returned an HTTP response. Use the status, request-id headers, and error body to check authentication, quota, model names, and API compatibility.
modelTestHint_dns: The server could not resolve the target hostname. Check the Base URL, server or container DNS configuration, and whether the hostname resolves from the deployment environment.
modelTestHint_connection_refused: The target host or proxy port refused the connection. Confirm the service is listening, the port is correct, firewalls allow it, and any configured proxy is reachable.
modelTestHint_connection_reset: The upstream, reverse proxy, or WAF closed the connection before returning an HTTP response. Check the actual endpoint path, proxy/WAF logs, body-size limits, TLS forwarding, and upstream stability.
modelTestHint_timeout: The connection or response timed out. Check network quality, proxy hops, upstream load, and timeout settings, then correlate the diagnostic time with upstream logs.
modelTestHint_tls: The TLS handshake or certificate validation failed. Check the certificate chain, hostname match, system clock, enterprise CA certificates, and HTTPS proxy settings.
modelTestHint_proxy: The request failed while using a proxy. Check the proxy URL, credentials, protocol, and destination policy; temporarily compare with a direct connection if appropriate.
modelTestHint_aborted: The request was cancelled before completion. If this was not manual, check navigation, server restarts, and higher-level timeouts that may trigger an AbortSignal.
modelTestHint_network: The request failed before any HTTP response arrived. Use the error code, actual URL, direct/proxy route, and server logs to continue diagnosing the transport failure.
webFetchProxyDesc: Proxy mode for WebFetch HTTP requests and browser page fetching.
storageChatAttachmentsDesc: Images and files posted in discussions and direct messages
storageWorktreesDesc: Git worktree directories for active chapters
storageTreeSnapshotsDesc: Content-addressed workspace states used for precise rollback
storageRequestDumpsDesc: Full API request/response captures too large for the database, kept so dumps download complete
storageDormantIgnoredDesc: Git-ignored files held for dormant chapters, restored when they wake
storageCleanupWorktreesRuntimeFallback: Remove orphaned worktrees through runtime cleanup
storageCleanupUnsupported: This cleanup action is not supported by the current backend.
storageCleanupUploadsUnsafe: Uploads cleanup is disabled because this backend cannot guarantee message image references are preserved.
storageCleanupConfirm: Are you sure? This action cannot be undone.
storageScanUnsupported: Storage scan is not supported by the current backend runtime.
storageNotScanned: Click Scan to analyze storage usage
storageDatabaseIncomplete: {{count}} table(s) could not be measured, usually because another operation (such as VACUUM) held the database lock. Their size counts as 0 here, so the totals below understate real usage. Rescan once maintenance finishes.
storageDatabaseIncompleteWithTables: {{count}} table(s) could not be measured ({{tables}}), usually because another operation (such as VACUUM) held the database lock. Their size counts as 0 here, so the totals below understate real usage. Rescan once maintenance finishes.
storageDatabaseUsageFreeStats: SQLite pages that are reusable but not yet returned to the filesystem
storageDatabaseVacuumDisabled: The current database backend does not support administrator-run VACUUM maintenance.
storageDatabaseVacuumConfirm: SQLite VACUUM runs synchronously and will freeze the ENTIRE backend — every user, every request, and all live sessions and terminals will hang until it finishes. On a multi-GB database this can take minutes. It also temporarily needs extra disk space (roughly the size of the database). Only run this during a maintenance window. Continue?
storageDatabaseVacuumSuccess: Database compaction completed, freed {{size}} (previous free pages {{freeBefore}}, {{duration}}s)
storageDatabaseArchivedSessionsDesc: Delete archived session trees that are no longer attached to chapters
storageDatabaseStaleSessionsDesc: By default, clean standalone sessions inactive for {{days}} days
storageDatabaseApiRequestDumpsDesc: By default, clear raw request/response dumps older than {{days}} days
storageDatabaseToolCallPayloadsDesc: By default, clear tool-call inputs/outputs older than {{days}} days. The records themselves are kept, so file-history revert keeps working; only the execution log's payload view is lost.
storageDatabasePreviewUnsupported: Database cleanup preview is not available in the current backend runtime.
storageDatabaseWillDeleteUsageHistory: Deleting sessions also deletes their linked usage history and request statistics.
storageDatabaseDumpEnabledNote: “Dump every API request” is currently enabled, so new dumps will continue to accumulate after cleanup.
storageDatabaseNoCandidates: There is nothing cleanable right now.
storageDatabaseCleanupUnsupported: Cleanup for this database target is not available in the current backend runtime.
workspaceBarriersDescription: Uncertain writes quarantine their actual file or subtree ranges, not unrelated files. Recovery is available only after execution is proven ended. Re-observe and confirm the complete preview before releasing a barrier.
workspaceBarriersExecutionUnknown: Execution is active or its owner is unknown
workspaceBarriersAlreadySettled: Already settled: this only compares current state; the original execution evidence is not reclassified.
workspaceBarriersEmpty: No barriers are waiting for recovery.
workspaceBarriersRemoteUnsupported: Recovery is only available on the server's local device
workspaceBarriersRecoverDisabled: Re-observe and confirm every verdict first
workspaceBarriersRecoverConfirm: This closes the evidence books for "{{root}}" with the verdicts you confirmed and lifts the write barrier. Physical files are never modified by recovery. Continue?
workspaceBarriersRecoverConfirmRoot: This re-measures the identity of "{{root}}" and marks it verified, lifting the write barrier. Continue?
workspaceBarriersForeignWarning: At least one file matches NEITHER its before state nor the intended write result — something else changed it. Open the file and verify its content yourself before confirming.
workspaceBarriersVerdictExplanation: Verdict: {{verdict}} — check the box to confirm you accept this verdict
workspaceBarriersInspectedLabel: I have inspected every displayed range, including directory contents not recursively scanned by this preview, and accept their current state.
storageDatabaseNothingToCleanup: There is nothing to clean right now
storageDatabaseBlockedReason_nonArchived: Contains descendant sessions that are not archived
storageDatabaseBlockedReason_nonStaleSta: Contains descendant sessions still considered active
runtimeNotScanned: Click Scan to check runtime resource usage
runtimeScanUnsupported: Runtime resource scanning is not available in this backend runtime.
runtimeTerminalsDesc: Terminal processes managed by the server
runtimeCleanupTerminals: Kill exited terminals and orphan sockets
runtimeCleanupTerminalsUnsupported: Terminal cleanup is not available in this backend runtime.
runtimeCleanupContainersUnsupported: Container cleanup is not available in this backend runtime.
runtimeBrowsersDesc: Chrome browser for web page fetching
runtimeCleanupBrowsers: Close all sessions and browser process
runtimeCleanupBrowsersUnsupported: Browser cleanup is not available in this backend runtime.
runtimeCleanupConfirm: Are you sure? This will terminate the selected resources.
runtimeCleanupPreviewOnly: Runtime cleanup returned a preview only; no resources were terminated.
providerRefreshModelsUnsupported: Refreshing model lists is not supported by this backend runtime.
providerRouteUnsupported: This route is not supported by this backend runtime.
providerQuotaUnsupported: Quota inspection is not available in this backend runtime.
pluginProviderNoCustomUi: This plugin does not ship its own settings view, so the configuration below is generated from the schema it declares.
pluginProviderConnectionDesc: Advanced non-secret provider settings are stored by NarraFork, separate from the plugin's own account page.
providerConfigDesc: Configure API credentials, model list, and advanced options.
gatewayDesc: Connect instant messaging platforms to NarraFork narrators. Each platform can be configured independently.
gatewayEnabledDesc: Allow IM platforms to send messages to narrators.
gatewayStreamingDesc: Progressively edit messages as the narrator generates text (requires platform edit support).
gatewayDefaultPermissionModeDesc: Permission mode for narrators created by IM sessions.
gatewaySessionIdleDesc: Auto-reset sessions after this many minutes of inactivity. 0 = never.
gatewayRateLimitDesc: Max messages per user per minute. 0 = unlimited.
gatewayDefaultProjectDesc: Bind new IM sessions to this project (optional).
gatewayDefaultChapterDesc: Bind new IM sessions to this chapter (optional).
gatewayPlatformAllowedUsersDesc: Comma-separated user IDs. Leave empty to allow all.
gatewayNoPlatforms: No platforms configured. Add one to get started.
gatewayPersistentRuntimesUnsupported: This backend only supports the webhook gateway fallback. Persistent IM gateway runtimes are not available here.
gatewayWeixinDesc: Connect a WeChat personal account via iLink Bot API. Requires QR code login.
gatewayWeixinQrScanning: Scan the QR code with WeChat
gatewayWeixinQrUnsupported: WeChat QR login is not supported by this backend/runtime.
gatewayWeixinAllowedUsersDesc: Comma-separated WeChat user IDs. Leave empty to allow all.
gatewayQQBotDesc: Connect a QQ Bot via the official QQ Bot API (v2). Requires App ID and Client Secret from the QQ Open Platform.
gatewayQQBotAppIdDesc: QQ Bot App ID from the QQ Open Platform.
gatewayQQBotClientSecretDesc: QQ Bot App Secret from the QQ Open Platform.
gatewayQQBotDmPolicyDesc: Control who can send direct messages to the bot.
gatewayQQBotGroupPolicyDesc: Control which groups the bot responds in.
gatewayQQBotAllowedUsersDesc: Comma-separated user OpenIDs for DM access. Only used when DM policy is "Allowlist".
gatewayQQBotAllowedGroupsDesc: Comma-separated group OpenIDs. Only used when group policy is "Allowlist".
gatewayQQBotMarkdownDesc: Send messages using QQ markdown format (msg_type 2).
gatewayQQBotSandboxDesc: Route requests to the QQ sandbox gateway for testing.
gatewayQQBotSttApiKeyDesc: API key for the external STT provider (e.g. Zhipu GLM-ASR).
gatewayQQBotSttBaseUrlDesc: Base URL for the STT API. Default: https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/coding/paas/v4
gatewayQQBotSttModelDesc: Model name for STT. Default: glm-asr
proxyManagementDesc: A single outbound proxy policy applied to every outbound network request.
proxyOutboundDesc: Controls the proxy for all outbound requests (AI providers and WebFetch). Defaults to a direct connection (no proxy).
proxyOverrideDesc: Override the global outbound proxy for this item.
proxyOverrideUrlCommitHint: Press Enter or click away to save
proxyOverridesDesc: Override the global proxy for individual providers, IM platforms, or hooks. "Follow global default" inherits the policy above.
proxyInvalidUrl: Enter a valid HTTP or HTTPS proxy URL
proxyScopeAiProviders: All AI providers (Codex, Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible, NUG)
proxyScopeWebFetch: WebFetch HTTP requests and the built-in browser
proxyScopeImGateway: IM gateway platforms (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, WeChat, QQ Bot)
proxyScopeImWsLimit: For Discord, Slack, and Feishu only REST/HTTP traffic is proxied; their event WebSocket connections may not go through the proxy (SDK limitation).
proxyScopeLoopbackExempt: Local / loopback targets and NO_PROXY entries are always reached directly.
proxyMovedToGlobalNote: Proxy is now configured globally in Settings → Proxy and applies to all outbound requests.
searchSectionDesc: Manage web search channels and priority across native model search, managed MCP search, custom search APIs, and search subagents.
searchChannelsDesc: Channels are tried in order. Native search only applies when it is the first enabled channel and the current model supports it.
oauthAppsDescription: Register third-party applications that users can authorize (NarraFork as the OAuth provider).
oauthAppsScopesHint: Grant only the minimum scopes the integration needs. Expand the authorization policy to further limit narrator and resource capabilities.
oauthAppsClientIdHint: Set a fixed Client ID if the third-party app requires one; leave blank to generate one.
oauthAppsRedirectUrisHint: One absolute URL per line. Must match the third-party app's redirect_uri exactly.
oauthAppsRevokeConfirm: Revoke {{name}}? The app will no longer be able to mint tokens, and its existing grants will stop working.
oauthAppsCreatedHint: Copy the Client ID. Public clients have no secret — third parties complete the flow with PKCE.
oauthAppsRedirectRequired: At least one redirect URI is required
connectedAppsDescription: Review and revoke third-party apps authorized to access your account.
connectedAppsRevokeConfirm: Revoke {{name}}'s access to your account? Its existing access and refresh tokens will stop working.
connectedAppsRevokeSelectedConfirm: Revoke access for the {{count}} selected apps? Their existing access and refresh tokens will stop working.
connectedAppsRevokeAllConfirm: Revoke access for all connected apps? Every existing OAuth access and refresh token for your account will stop working.
oauthAppsPolicyDescription: Limit how this client may use narrators, system prompts, devices, and knowledge-base access.
oauthAppsPolicyDefaultPermissionModeDesc: Permission mode applied when the client does not request an allowed override.
oauthAppsPolicyAllowedPermissionModesDes: Modes this client may request. The default mode must remain selected.
oauthAppsPolicyPermissionModeReadOnlyDes: Allow reading and analysis without file edits or command execution.
oauthAppsPolicyPermissionModeDontAskDesc: Reject operations that require interactive approval instead of prompting the user.
oauthAppsPolicySystemPromptModeDesc: Control whether the client may add content to NarraFork's managed system prompt.
oauthAppsPolicySystemPromptModeManagedDe: Ignore client-supplied system prompt content and use only the NarraFork-managed prompt.
oauthAppsPolicySystemPromptModeAppendDes: Append bounded client-supplied content after the NarraFork-managed prompt.
oauthAppsPolicyMaxSystemPromptCharsDesc: Maximum appended system prompt length from 0 to 10,000 characters. Use 0 to disable client-supplied prompt content.
oauthAppsPolicyAllowGlobalDeviceDesc: Permit device operations that are not restricted to the projects selected in the user's grant.
oauthAppsPolicyAllowKnowledgeWriteDesc: Permit this client to create or modify knowledge-base content when the granted scopes also allow it.
oauthAppsPolicyRemoteDiagnosticsDesc: These capabilities only apply to remote devices this client registered and owns, and are enabled by default. Turn them off below to restrict this client. The NarraFork host itself is never affected by these switches and remains off-limits.
oauthAppsPolicyAllowRemoteShellDesc: Permit narrators owned by this client to run shell commands on its bound remote device. Enabled by default; turn off here to restrict this client.
oauthAppsPolicyRemoteShellLevelDesc: Read only rejects commands with write operations. Read write allows commands accepted by the remote safety policy.
oauthAppsPolicyAllowRemoteFileWriteDesc: Permit narrators owned by this client to write or edit files on its bound remote device. Enabled by default; local host paths remain blocked.
oauthAppsPolicyInvalidDefaultPermissionM: Select a valid default permission mode
oauthAppsPolicyInvalidAllowedPermissionM: Select at least one allowed permission mode
oauthAppsPolicyDefaultMustBeAllowed: The default permission mode must also be allowed
oauthAppsPolicyInvalidMaxSystemPromptCha: Enter a whole number from 0 to 10,000
oauthAppsPolicyInvalidDeviceAccess: Select a valid access level for every device group
oauthAppsPolicyDeviceAccessDesc: Set the maximum Bash, Write, and Edit access independently for the NarraFork host, global devices, and devices registered by this client.
oauthAppsPolicyInvalidMessageDetail: Select a valid message detail level
oauthAppsPolicyMessageDetailDesc: Highest level of message data this app may read. It still needs the matching scope, and the user still has to consent to it.
oauthAppsPolicyMessageDetailNoneDesc: Structured reads are refused. The app can still read bounded plain message text through narrator.read.
oauthAppsPolicyMessageDetailSummaryDesc: Message structure with identity: text, reasoning step titles, and each tool call's name, target, and status. No tool payloads.
oauthAppsPolicyMessageDetailFullDesc: Also exposes reasoning bodies and tool inputs and outputs. Payloads can contain commands, file contents, and other sensitive data.
oauthAppsImportDescription: Paste a NarraFork OAuth Client Manifest v1. An active app with the same client_id is synchronized; revoked apps are never reactivated automatically.
oauthAppsExportDescription: This manifest contains only portable OAuth registration data. It never includes tokens, secrets, or server-internal metadata.
oauthExternalWebSocketAdvancedHint: Low-frequency runtime settings, collapsed by default. Adjust only when deploying third-party real-time clients.
oauthExternalWebSocketDescription: Configure the isolated real-time narrator channel for third-party OAuth clients.
oauthExternalWebSocketInfo: The endpoint is always enabled. Each capability (subscribe, send messages, interrupt) is authorized by OAuth scopes and grants, so no feature toggles are needed. The fields below only tune operational limits such as ticket lifetime, connection caps, and buffering.
oauthExternalWebSocketAllowedOriginsHint: One exact HTTP(S) origin per line, without a path. An empty list rejects browser clients that send Origin; non-browser clients may omit it.
oauthExternalWebSocketSaveFailed: Failed to save external OAuth WebSocket settings
traitLayerProjectDesc: Applies to every narrator in this project. Narrators may tighten these further, and may only loosen the ones not marked as enforced.
traitLayerProjectIntro: These settings apply to all narrators in this project. They sit above each narrator's own settings, so a narrator can add restrictions but can only remove the ones that are not enforced.
traitLayerUserDesc: Applies to every narrator you work with, across all projects. Project and narrator settings sit above these.
traitLayerUserIntro: These are your personal defaults, applied to every narrator you drive. Project policy and each narrator's own settings take precedence.
traitLayerToolRestrictionDesc: Tools listed here are hidden from the model. Restrictions accumulate across layers.
traitLayerSkillRestrictionDesc: Blocked skills are not offered and cannot be loaded manually.
traitLayerSkillsPlaceholder: Type a skill name and press Enter
traitLayerEnforcedHelp: When enforced, this restriction is a boundary: narrators and lower levels can add to it but never remove it. When not enforced, it is only a default that they may override.
traitLayerDeviceInjectionDesc: Controls which authorized devices are described to the model. This does not change what a device is allowed to do — it only limits how much the model is told, which keeps unused machines out of the context.
traitLayerInjectionMode: Default for devices with no explicit setting
traitLayerInjectionAll: All authorized devices, including project ones
traitLayerInjectionNone: None (each device must be turned on)
traitLayerPerDeviceDesc: Per-device override. "Inherit" follows the default above.
modelCardsDesc: A card is a reusable template for one model: context window, max completion tokens, reasoning tiers and official reference prices. Fields left empty inherit NarraFork's builtin values, and only your changes are saved — so untouched fields keep tracking builtin updates across releases.
modelCardKeyDesc: Normalized to a lower-case match key, e.g. gpt-5.6-sol
modelCardMatchRulesDesc: Priority: exact key → alias → with date/snapshot suffix stripped (-2026-01-01 / -latest / -preview) → prefixes. Prefixes rank last and the longest one wins. Semantic suffixes such as -mini or -thinking are never stripped, so a variant never inherits its base model's values.
modelCardAliasesDesc: Exact alternate keys; press Enter to add
modelCardMatchPrefixesDesc: Any model id starting with this matches the card
modelCardEffortLevelsDesc: Ascending order, low to high. Leave empty to inherit. "none" (thinking off) is added by the UI and cannot be set here.
modelCardPriceCacheWriteDesc: 0 = the vendor charges no separate cache-write fee
modelCardResetTooltip: Discard your changes and follow the builtin values again
modelCardResetConfirm: Discard your changes to {{model}} and follow the builtin values again?
modelCardDeleteConfirm: Delete the model card for {{model}}? Its pricing, context window and matching rules are not recoverable.
narratorTypographyDesc: Applies to conversation text only. A Typography panel inside each conversation offers the same controls next to live content.
narratorFontScaleDesc: Scales body text, headings, code and labels together.
narratorLetterSpacingDesc: Extra space between characters, as a share of the font size.
narratorParagraphScaleDesc: Gaps between paragraphs, lists, code blocks and messages.
narratorLineHeightDesc: Spacing between lines inside a paragraph.
